dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a natural number m and finite type Omega, this is the inductive type of admissible runs. Its constructor bundles a probability distribution, positive naturals p and r, coefficients a, perturbations delta and beta, a truncation function, and the conditions listed in D011.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target is universal over admissible runs, so every condition bundled by this type is an implicit hypothesis of the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the coefficient vector a from a run; it is a function Fin (m+1) -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the m+1 exact summands used in the exact sum, computed recurrence, and condition factor.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the natural number p from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with r, p determines the perturbation scales; the constructor also requires p>0.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the natural number r from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The final bound uses the scale indexed by p+r; the constructor requires r>0.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a : Fin n -> Real, this is the finite sum sum_i a(i) over every i in Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the run's coefficient vector it is the exact sum A=sum_{i=0}^m a_i, which appears in both denominators and in the error numerator.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the expectation, under the run's finite probability distribution, of the recursively perturbed sum obtained from a and delta by D014.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the expected computed result whose relative difference from the exact sum is bounded.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n : Nat and u : Real, this is (1+u)^n-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With n=m and u=(1/2)^((p+r)-1), it is the growth factor on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a : Fin n -> Real, this is (sum_i |a_i|)/|sum_i a_i|, using totalized real division.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the coefficient-sum condition factor multiplying the growth factor; the target's nonzero-sum hypothesis makes its denominator nonzero.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: For q : Nat, this is u_q=(1/2)^(q-1), where q-1 is natural-number subtraction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It bounds delta at q=p, bounds beta at q=p+r, and supplies u_{p+r} in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects delta : Fin m -> Omega -> Real from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Delta drives the recursive computed sum and is constrained by the run's pointwise bounds and moment conditions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructor builds a run from a finite probability model, p,r>0, a : Fin (m+1) -> Real, delta,beta : Fin m -> Omega -> Real, and truncate : Real -> Real, assuming |delta_k|<=u_p, 0<=1+delta_k, |beta_k|<=u_{p+r}, truncate(q_k)=q_k(1+beta_k), q_k=0 implies both delta_k=0 and beta_k=0, beta_k depends only on earlier deltas, and E[X delta_k]=E[X beta_k] for every X depending only on earlier deltas.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These conditions are all encoded in the quantified run even though the displayed target explicitly names only the run and the nonzero exact-sum hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the finite probability distribution from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the weights used to define the expectation of the computed result and all moment identities.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite probability model P and X : Omega -> Real, this is E_P[X]=sum_{omega in Omega} P.prob(omega) X(omega).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the expected computed value and the weighted moment equations imposed by the run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: Starting from x_0=a_0, this left fold processes k=0,...,m-1 by x_{k+1}=(x_k+a_{k+1})(1+delta_k), and returns x_m.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied pointwise in omega, it is the random recursively perturbed sum whose expectation occurs in the error.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: This proves that the natural number 1+1 satisfies the AtLeastTwo certificate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports elaboration of the real numeral 2 used in 1/2 and adds no mathematical hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: For finite Omega, this is the type of finite probability distributions, constructed from nonnegative real weights whose total is 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every run carries such a normalized nonnegative distribution for its expectations.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the probability-mass function prob : Omega -> Real from a finite probability distribution.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These values are the weights in every expectation.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef018 delta k X says that X depends only on delta_j for j<k: if two outcomes agree on all such earlier perturbations, then X has the same value at those outcomes.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses adaptedness of beta_k and identifies the class of test functions X for which the delta_k and beta_k weighted moments must agree.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019
dependency_coverage.meaning: For step k, this is q_k=x_k+a_{k+1}, where x_k is the partial recurrence through the preceding steps.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the pre-perturbation value at which the truncation equation and zero-consistency conditions are imposed.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020
dependency_coverage.meaning: This proves that m+1 is nonzero for every natural m.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits use of index 0 in Fin (m+1), especially for a_0, without adding an assumption.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructs a finite probability distribution from prob : Omega -> Real when every prob(omega)>=0 and sum_omega prob(omega)=1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures the expectation weights bundled in a run are nonnegative and normalized.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef022
dependency_coverage.meaning: For step k, this folds the recurrence over exactly the earlier indices j<k, starting at a_0; its value is x_k.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Adding a_{k+1} gives the pre-perturbation quantity q_k used in the run conditions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef023
dependency_coverage.meaning: For k : Fin m and j : Fin k.val, this proves j.val<m.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It justifies embedding each earlier fold index into Fin m and has no additional mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the division operation from a DivInvMonoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real it supplies ordinary totalized real division in the relative error, condition factor, and 1/2.

dependency_coverage.name: Fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: A Fintype instance equips a type with a finite enumeration containing all its elements.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes Omega finite and allows sums over all outcomes and all finite indices.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the addition operation supplied by an HAdd instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It realizes natural additions such as m+1 and p+r and real additions in the recurrence and growth factor.

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the division operation supplied by an HDiv instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It realizes the real quotients in the relative error, condition factor, and unit-roundoff definition.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the multiplication operation supplied by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It realizes recurrence products, weighted expectations, and the product of the two right-hand-side factors.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the subtraction operation supplied by an HSub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the expected-minus-exact error and the subtraction of 1 in the growth and exponent definitions.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the non-strict order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real it expresses all pointwise bounds and the final inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes the number of recurrence steps, precisions p and r, finite dimensions, and natural exponents.

dependency_coverage.name: Ne
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ne a b means not (a=b).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It states that the exact coefficient sum A is not zero.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets a natural-number literal in a type having the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the literals 0, 1, and 2 used throughout the definitions.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All coefficients, perturbations, probabilities, expectations, errors, and bounds are real-valued.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the additive-group structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides negation and additive structure needed for real subtraction and absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instDivInvMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the standard multiplicative, inverse, and division structure on Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the real division used by the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the standard less-than-or-equal relation on Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The conclusion and all real-valued bounds use the usual real order.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies standard real multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines every real product in the recurrence, expectation, and bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies real subtraction, defined as addition of the additive inverse.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the error E[x_m]-A and the real expression (1+u)^m-1.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the real number zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is used in the nonzero-sum hypothesis and the run's zero and nonnegativity conditions.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the lattice order structure on Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with the additive group, it defines the usual real absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns a Zero instance into interpretation of the numeral 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the displayed real zero denote the standard real zero.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: In a lattice-ordered additive group, abs(a)=max(a,-a); for Real this is the usual absolute value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It measures the error, exact-sum denominator, coefficient magnitudes, and perturbation magnitudes.

dependency_coverage.name: instAddNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies ordinary natural-number addition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes m+1 and p+r the usual natural sums.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This converts a homogeneous Add operation into the corresponding HAdd operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It routes natural and real additions to their standard addition instances.

dependency_coverage.name: instHDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This converts a homogeneous Div operation into the corresponding HDiv operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It routes all real quotients to real division.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This converts a homogeneous Mul operation into the corresponding HMul operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It routes all real products to real multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This converts a homogeneous Sub operation into the corresponding HSub operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It routes natural and real subtractions to their respective subtraction operations.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets every natural literal n as the natural number n itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the standard meanings to natural literals such as 0 and 1.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type consisting of natural numbers strictly less than n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes the m+1 coefficients, the m perturbation steps, and finite folds.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the canonical finite enumeration of Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It allows sums over all coefficient indices.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: This sums a function over a finite set in an additive commutative monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines coefficient sums, sums of coefficient magnitudes, normalization of probabilities, and finite expectations.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite type, this is the finite set containing every element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each relevant sum range over all indices or all outcomes.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the exponentiation operation supplied by an HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms (1+u)^m and (1/2)^(q-1).

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies natural-number exponentiation in a monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real it gives the standard nonnegative-integer powers used in the perturbation scale and growth factor.

dependency_coverage.name: One.toOfNat1
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns a One instance into interpretation of the numeral 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the standard real one in 1/2, 1+delta, 1+beta, and the growth factor.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies standard real addition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines additions in the recurrence and expressions of the form 1+u.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the additive commutative monoid structure of Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports all finite sums of real values.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the multiplicative monoid structure of Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports natural powers of real bases.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNatCast
dependency_coverage.meaning: This embeds natural numbers into the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets real numerals at least 2, in particular the denominator 2 in 1/2.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instOne
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the multiplicative identity 1 in Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines every occurrence of real one.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This converts a Pow operation into the corresponding homogeneous HPow operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It routes real bases with natural exponents to standard real natural powers.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatAtLeastTwo
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a natural-cast operation and an AtLeastTwo certificate, this interprets a natural numeral as its cast.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real numeral 2 used in the unit-roundoff base 1/2.

dependency_coverage.name: instSubNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies truncated natural-number subtraction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes q-1 in u_q=(1/2)^(q-1) a natural exponent, with values below zero truncated to zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is propositional equality.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses probability normalization, truncation equations, zero implications, agreement of histories, and equality of weighted moments.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.foldl
dependency_coverage.meaning: This left-folds a function over the finite indices 0 through n-1, beginning with a supplied initial value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines both the complete recurrence x_m and each partial value x_k.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.instOfNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: When n is nonzero, this interprets a natural literal as an element of Fin n via the canonical finite-index conversion.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the index 0 in Fin (m+1) for the initial coefficient a_0.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.succ
dependency_coverage.meaning: For k : Fin n, this constructs the index with value k.val+1 in Fin (n+1).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It selects coefficient a_{k+1} at recurrence step k.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the strict order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For naturals it expresses p>0, r>0, and the earlier-index condition j<k.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.AtLeastTwo
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the proposition-valued certificate used by numeral-cast machinery for natural numerals that are at least two.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is used only to authorize the real numeral 2 and imposes no hypothesis on the quantified run.

dependency_coverage.name: instLTNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies ordinary strict less-than on natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the standard meanings to positivity and earlier-index comparisons.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.val
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the underlying natural value of a finite index.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is used to compare finite indices and determine the length of each partial fold.

dependency_coverage.name: NeZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: NeZero n is bundled evidence that n is not the zero element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For n=m+1 it permits construction of the finite index 0.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.ofOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructs a Zero instance from an interpretation of the numeral 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the nonzero certificate machinery for natural finite-index sizes.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.mk
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a natural value i and a proof i<n, this constructs the corresponding element of Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It embeds earlier indices into the full step-index type when defining partial recurrences.

binders: m is an arbitrary natural number, including zero.
Omega is an arbitrary type equipped with a finite enumeration.

run is an arbitrary admissible run bundling a finite probability mass function pi, positive naturals p and r, coefficients a : Fin (m+1) -> Real, perturbations delta,beta : Fin m -> Omega -> Real, a function T : Real -> Real, and proofs of the run conditions.
hypotheses: For every omega, pi(omega)>=0, and sum_{omega in Omega} pi(omega)=1.
For every k in Fin m and omega in Omega, |delta_k(omega)|<=u_p and 0<=1+delta_k(omega).
For every k and omega, q_k(omega)=0 implies delta_k(omega)=0 and beta_k(omega)=0.
For every k, beta_k depends only on the preceding perturbations delta_j with j<k.
For every k and every X : Omega -> Real that depends only on delta_j for j<k, E_pi[X delta_k]=E_pi[X beta_k].
The exact sum A=sum_{i=0}^m a_i is nonzero.
mathematical_definitions: Fin n is identified with the indices {0,...,n-1}; thus a has entries a_0,...,a_m and delta,beta have step indices 0,...,m-1.
u_q=(1/2)^(q-1), with q-1 evaluated by natural-number subtraction.
For each omega, x_0(omega)=a_0 and x_{k+1}(omega)=(x_k(omega)+a_{k+1})(1+delta_k(omega)) for k=0,...,m-1.
A function X is adapted before step k when agreement of two outcomes on every delta_j with j<k forces equal X-values.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite probability model and every admissible m-step perturbed summation run satisfying the stated pointwise, truncation, adaptedness, and moment-matching conditions, if the exact sum of the m+1 real coefficients is nonzero, then the relative absolute bias of the expected recursively perturbed result is at most the coefficient factor (sum of coefficient magnitudes divided by the magnitude of the exact sum) times (1+u_{p+r})^m-1.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The assertion is conditional on A being nonzero; it makes no claim when the exact coefficient sum is zero.
Real division is totalized in Lean, but the explicit A!=0 hypothesis ensures both displayed denominators are mathematically nonzero.

The theorem quantifies over inhabitants of the admissible-run type and does not assert that such a run exists for arbitrary m and Omega or arbitrary raw data. In particular, a normalized probability distribution cannot be constructed on an empty finite Omega.
The case m=0 is included. Then there are no perturbation steps and all hypotheses quantified over k : Fin 0 are vacuous.
Natural subtraction is truncated. The constructor assumptions p>0 and r>0 ensure p-1 and (p+r)-1 have their ordinary nonnegative values, with p+r>=2.
The conclusion bounds |E_pi[x_m]-A|, the absolute bias of the expected result. It does not bound E_pi[|x_m-A|], a pointwise error, a tail probability, or a high-probability error.
No independence assumptions are encoded. The only stochastic relation between delta_k and beta_k is equality of their weighted moments against every function determined by earlier deltas.

No equation identifies the recurrence output q_k(1+delta_k) with T(q_k). The supplied truncation equation uses beta_k, and delta_k is connected to beta_k only through zero consistency, adaptedness, and the stated moment identities.
The function T is otherwise arbitrary, and its behavior is constrained only at the encountered values q_k(omega).
No floating-point format, radix interpretation, overflow, underflow, exceptional values, or tie-breaking behavior is encoded beyond the explicit real-valued perturbation equations and bounds.
There is no smallness condition such as m*u_{p+r}<1; the bound uses the exact factor (1+u_{p+r})^m-1.
